bib.title: Florence: A New Foundation Model for Computer Vision

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Florence: A New Foundation Model for Computer Vision", Lu Yuan, Dongdong Chen, Yi-Ling Chen, Noel Codella, Xiyang Dai, Jianfeng Gao, Houdong Hu, Xuedong Huang, Boxin Li, Chunyuan Li, Ce Liu, Mengchen Liu, Zicheng Liu, Yumao Lu, Yu Shi, Lijuan Wang, Jianfeng Wang, Bin Xiao, Zhen Xiao, Jianwei Yang, Michael Zeng, Luowei Zhou, Pengchuan Zhang (Microsoft Cloud and AI / Microsoft Research). Preprint, arXiv:2111.11432v1, 22 Nov 2021.

COVERAGE: I read all 72,268 of 72,268 characters across 17 pages, covering sections 1 to 4, Tables 1 to 10, acknowledgments and references. The references were skimmed. The paper has no appendix and no limitations section. The PDF is /Users/ramsey-wise/workspace/learn-ai-engineering/ai-engineering/08-multimodal-engineering/sources/yuan-2021-florence.pdf.

CHECK AGAINST THE NOTE: The 80.2% in 01-image-input.md matches Florence's VQAv2 **test-dev** score of 80.16, so it is correct. The abstract's "80.36 on VQA" is the **test-std** figure, so the two splits should not be mixed. Florence's own 80.16 comes from the METER adapter (CoSwin-H plus RoBERTa with co-attention), pretrained on 14M images and fine-tuned on VQA. It is not the contrastive model by itself.

CLAIMS
- claim: The core claim is that one image-text pretrained model, plus light adapters, reaches state of the art on most of 44 benchmarks along three axes: space (scene to object), time (image to video) and modality.
  number: majority of 44 benchmarks
  setup: CoSwin-H plus a 12-layer text transformer trained on FLD-900M, with Dynamic Head, METER and Video CoSwin adapters
  quote: "Florence achieves new state-of-the-art re- sults in majority of 44 representative benchmarks"
  where: p1, abstract
- claim: Zero-shot ImageNet-1K top-1 is 83.74%, and Florence wins 9 of 12 zero-shot classification datasets.
  number: 83.74 top-1 / 97.18 top-5
  setup: CLIP prompt templates and ensembling; CoSwin-H at 384px; near-duplicate test images removed from training data; Birdsnap dropped because 20% of its URLs are dead. Table 1 compares against CLIP-ViT-L/14@336 (76.2) and FILIP-ViT-L/14 (78.3).
  quote: "the top-1 accu- racy of 83.74% (+5.6% over SOTA result), and the top-5 accuracy of 97.18%."
  where: p7, sec 3.1; Table 1 p6
- claim: The training data, FLD-900M, holds 900M image-text pairs filtered from about 3B web images.
  number: 900M pairs; ~3B source images; 9.7M unique queries; 7.5B tokens
  setup: The filtering follows ALIGN (hash near-dedup, small-image removal, image-text relevance). Sampling follows CLIP and DALL-E for balance. The dataset is not released.
  quote: "processes around 3 billion Internet images and their raw descriptions in parallel" / "900M images with 900M free-form texts (ranging from one word, phase to sentences), 9.7M unique queries, and 7.5B tokens in total."
  where: p3, sec 2.1
- claim: UniCL counts every image that shares an identical caption as a positive, instead of CLIP's one positive per image. This matters because 350M of the pairs share text with other images.
  number: 350M pairs
  setup: Triplets (x, t, y) are built with a text hash table, and the loss is a bidirectional supervised contrastive loss L = Li2t + Lt2i
  quote: "in FLD-900M, there are 350M image-text pairs where there are more than one im- ages corresponding to one identical text, and all images associated with the same text can be treated as positive pairs"
  where: p3, sec 2.2
- claim: Model size and training compute.
  number: 893M params (256M text, 637M CoSwin-H); 10 days on 512 A100-40GB
  setup: Two-tower model. CoSwin is Swin with CvT convolutional embeddings and global average pooling.
  quote: "Our Florence pretrained model has in total 893M parameters, including the language transformer with 256M parameters and the CoSwin-H transformer with 637M parameters. The model takes 10 days to train on 512 NVIDIA-A100 GPUs with 40GB memory per GPU."
  where: p4, sec 2.3
- claim: Training schedule: first with augmented prompts, then without them, then at higher resolution.
  number: 1M + 180K iterations; batch 24,576; 224px; then 80K iterations at 384px
  setup: AdamW; text truncated to 76 tokens
  quote: "We trained 1M it- erations in the ﬁrst stage, and continuously trained 180K iterations in the second stage." / "The batch size is 24, 576. We further trained 80K iterations at a higher resolution of 384× 384"
  where: p4, sec 2.2
- claim: Zero-shot image-text retrieval matches or beats all prior zero-shot results (relevant to 03-multimodal-rag).
  number: Flickr30K I→T 90.9 / T→I 76.7 R@1; MSCOCO 64.7 / 47.2 R@1
  setup: Cosine similarity between the separate tower embeddings, ranked over the test set. Flickr30K uses the 1K test set and MSCOCO the 5K test set. CLIP zero-shot MSCOCO scores are 58.4/37.8.
  quote: "image retrieval zero-shot ( 90.9/76.7 R@1 on Flickr30K image-to-text / text-to-image, 64.7/47.2 R@1 on MSCOCO image-to-text / text-to-image)"
  where: p3; Table 5 p9
- claim: Fine-tuned retrieval scores, reached with far fewer epochs than ALIGN.
  number: Flickr30K 97.2/87.9; MSCOCO 81.8/63.2 R@1; ~6% and 8% of ALIGN's epochs
  setup: Batch 3,072, 12 epochs, peak LR 2e-5
  quote: "our ﬁne tuning on retrieval is more efﬁcient, with only roughly 6% and 8% ﬁne-tuning epochs of ALIGN (Jia et al., 2021) on Flickr30k and MSCOCO respectively."
  where: p9, sec 3.5
- claim: VQAv2 sets a new state of the art, beating SimVLM while using less data.
  number: 80.16 test-dev / 80.36 test-std (SimVLM 80.03/80.34)
  setup: METER adapter with CoSwin-H and RoBERTa. VLP on 14M images / 20M captions (COCO, CC, CC12M, SBU, VG) for 43 epochs at 384px with ITM and MLM, then 10 epochs of VQA fine-tuning at LR 8e-6, scored as a 3,129-answer classifier
  quote: "Florence 80.16 80.36" / "Compared with SimVLM (Wang et al., 2021), which uses 1.8B image-text pairs, we only use900M data to pre-train the image encoder and 20M for VLP"
  where: p11, Table 8, sec 3.7
- claim: Linear probing wins 9 of 11 datasets; the losses are on 32x32 CIFAR.
  number: 9/11
  setup: CLIP linear-eval protocol; the reimplementation was checked to within ±0.1 of CLIP's reported numbers
  quote: "linear probe in 11 classiﬁcation downstream tasks (win 9/11)"
  where: p3; Table 2 p7
- claim: Fine-tuned ImageNet-1K comes slightly below CoAtNet-7, which is about 3x larger in both model and data.
  number: 90.05 top-1 / 99.02 top-5
  setup: Uses the pretraining loss with class names fed to the text encoder; 512px, batch 8,192, 10 epochs
  quote: "Florence-CoSwin-H 637M 900M 90.05 99.02" / "Our result is slightly worse than SOTA (Dai et al., 2021c), but their model and data scale are both 3× larger."
  where: p8, Table 3
- claim: Object detection with the Dynamic Head adapter, pretrained on FLOD-9M.
  number: COCO test-dev 62.4 mAP; Object365 39.3; VG 16.2 AP50
  setup: FLOD-9M has 8,967,286 images, 25,190 categories and 33.4M boxes (including ImageNet-22K pseudo-labels). Pretraining ran 12 epochs on 128 A100s for 7 days, using multi-scale training and testing.
  quote: "object detection (62.4 mAP on COCO, 39.3 mAP on Ob- ject365, 16.2 AP50 on Visual Genome)" / "takes 7 days on 128 NVIDIA-A100 GPUs."
  where: p3, p5, Table 6 p10
- claim: Zero-shot detection on 11 Roboflow datasets beats 5-shot fine-tuning on 7 of the 11, but stays well below full supervision on new domains.
  number: 7/11; Packages 79.6 vs full fine-tune 52.0
  setup: Frozen CoSwin. Dynamic Head is trained as a class-agnostic proposer and each box is then classified zero-shot.
  quote: "Florence outperforms in 7/11 tasks over 5-shot ﬁne tun- ing, and outperforms full-set ﬁne-tuning on the “Packages” dataset, consisting of only 26 images for training."
  where: p10-11, Table 7
- claim: Cross-domain few-shot scores edge out the CD-FSL 2020 winner using a single model and no transduction.
  number: mean 74.8 vs 73.9
  setup: 5-way classification at 5/20/50 shots over 600 episodes, linear head, 100 epochs per episode
  quote: "The average result comparison is 74.8 (Florence) vs. 73.9 (CW)."
  where: p8, Table 4
- claim: Video results: zero-shot MSR-VTT retrieval and fine-tuned Kinetics.
  number: MSR-VTT 1K-A R@1 37.6 (CLIP-ViT-B/16 26.0); K400 86.5, K600 87.8 top-1
  setup: Video CoSwin inflates the 2D weights to 3D. Kinetics is fine-tuned at 384px for 30 epochs, evaluated with 4×3 views, 647M params.
  quote: "text-to-video retrieval zero-shot (37.6 R@1 on MSR-VTT), and video action recognition (top-1 accuracy 86.5/87.8 on Kinetics-400 / Kinetics-600)."
  where: p3; Tables 9-10 p12

ABLATIONS: The paper has no ablation tables, no ablation numbers and no comparison of UniCL against plain CLIP loss. Only two findings are stated qualitatively, and neither has numbers.
- "long language de- scriptions with rich content would be more beneﬁcial for image-text representation learning than short descriptions" (p4)
- "Although including generated language prompt might not affect classiﬁcation accuracy, it hurts the performance in retrieval and vision- language tasks." This is the stated reason for the two-stage schedule (p4).
Figure 5, on GPU memory with and without ZeRO, checkpointing, mixed precision and gradient cache, is a systems profile, not an accuracy ablation.

LIMITS:
- FLD-900M and FLOD-9M are in-house and unreleased. The curation is described only in outline ("respecting legal and ethical constraints").
- There are no seeds, error bars or repeat runs; every number comes from a single run.
- Compute is large (512 A100s for 10 days, plus 128 A100s for 7 days for detection), with no carbon or cost figure.
- The authors concede the model "is still below several other existing billion-scale models" in size. They also concede zero-shot detection "still has a long way to be applied to real-world tasks", with a gap to supervision on new concepts (BCCD, Chess).
- The VQA result depends on a separate 14M-image VLP stage, not the contrastive model alone.
- The UniCL citation (Yang et al., 2022) is "In Preparation".
- Depth, flow and tracking appear in Figure 1 but are not evaluated; they are listed as future work.
- Dated: this is a v1 preprint from 2021. The state-of-the-art claims are against 2021 baselines.

BUILDS ON (as printed): CLIP (Radford et al., 2021); ALIGN (Jia et al., 2021) for filtering; UniCL (Yang et al., 2022); Swin (Liu et al., 2021a) and CvT (Wu et al., 2021) for CoSwin; Dynamic Head (Dai et al., 2021a); METER (Dou et al., 2021); Video Swin (Liu et al., 2021b); ZeRO (Rajbhandari et al., 2019); Gradient Cache (Gao et al., 2021); sampling from Radford et al., 2021 and Ramesh et al., 2021; pseudo-boxes following Zoph et al., 2020; foundation-model term from Bommasani et al., 2021.

CODE: None. The only formula is the UniCL loss (eq. 2, p4); the extraction mangles it. Li2t = −Σ_{i∈B} 1/|P(i)| Σ_{k∈P(i)} log [exp(τ u_i v_k) / Σ_{j∈B} exp(τ u_i v_j)], where P(i) = {k | k∈B, y_k = y_i}. Lt2i is the mirror form over Q(j).

FIGURES:
- Fig 2 (p2), "Overview of building Florence": a single diagram showing data curation, then UniCL two-tower pretraining, then three adapters. It shows the backbone-plus-adapters idea faster than prose.
- Fig 1 (p1), the Space-Time-Modality task cube. It frames what "foundation" means here.
- Fig 4 (p5), the METER co-attention adapter. It shows how the VQA number was produced, not by the contrastive towers alone.
- Fig 5 (p6), GPU memory against batch size with and without the optimisations.
- Fig 3 (p5) Dynamic Head and Fig 6 (p10) detection examples are lower value.

PROBLEMS:
- The text says "+5.6% over SOTA", but Table 1's best prior ImageNet score is FILIP at 78.3, which gives +5.4. The baseline behind 5.6 is unclear.
- The text names the comparison "FILIP" while the tables label it "FLIP".
- Table 1 lists ImageNet as 83.7 while the text gives 83.74.
- Section 3.7 refers to "Figure 8" for VQA results; it means Table 8.
- The equations extract with broken layout.
- No embedded instructions were found. The text extraction was otherwise clean.
